certificate.reason: pure measurement run: no discrete log is claimed, no factor-base relation is claimed, no isogeny is computed, and no instance of any hard problem is solved.  docs/claims-and-verification.md requires kind: none to be stated explicitly.

C_ANCHOR_HIGH.primes_skipped_reason: floor((p/2)^(1/3)) < 1: no integer threshold to anchor
C_ANCHOR_HIGH.rule: fraction(T = floor((p/2)^(1/3))) = 1 for every covered prime, i.e. max delta_E <= floor((p/2)^(1/3))

C_ANCHOR_LOW.preregistered_criterion: N(1,p) reproduces the F_p-rational supersingular locus, 'known to be ~ p^{1/2}'.  Applied as: the OLS slope of log N(1,p) on log p over every covered prime lies in 0.5 +- 0.10.
C_ANCHOR_LOW.primes_skipped_reason: p <= 3: the class-number identity and the p^{1/2} scaling are stated for p > 3
C_ANCHOR_LOW.supplementary_exact_identity_rule: N(1,p) = #{E : delta_E = 1} = #{supersingular j-invariants in F_p} = h(-4p)/2, h = class number of the order of discriminant -4p.  Stronger than the pre-registered check and NOT pre-registered; recorded separately.

C_NULL.consequence: PRIMARY METRIC VOID: the measurement does not distinguish supersingular arithmetic from generic ternary lattice geometry, so M-ALPHA may not be cited as evidence about D1 (spec controls C-NULL failure_consequence).
C_NULL.criterion_used: the surrogate 'reproduces' a component if |data - null| <= 0.20 for alpha and beta (the contract's own exponent tolerance) and <= ln 2 for log c (a bounded factor of 2).  THE FROZEN CONTRACT FIXES NO NUMERIC TOLERANCE FOR c; this criterion is stated here so the recorded numbers can be re-read under a different tolerance without re-running.  It does not affect alpha.
C_NULL.surrogate: random ternary lattices L_v = {x in Z^3 : <x,v> = 0 mod q}, v uniform with gcd(v,q)=1, q = round(sqrt(p)/2), so the Gram determinant is q^2 ~= p/4; N1_null = min nonzero |x|^2.  Identical estimator, identical window.

compared: alpha, beta, log c and their standard errors for W-MAIN and W-SENS
the three per-seed C-NULL alpha/beta/log c
C_REPRO.provenance: written by implementation-adjacent post-step attach_repro.py, which only reads and compares the COEFFICIENT_DIGEST/COEFFICIENT_KEY lines emitted by fit_delta_counting.py in the two executions of this run; it computes no new quantity
C_REPRO.rule: re-run the full pipeline from the fetched bytes with the recorded seeds and confirm bit-identical fitted coefficients

C_SEED.applies_to: C-NULL surrogate (measured) and the M-GRAD arm (not measured, see M_GRAD)
C_SEED.criterion_used: pass iff the C-NULL verdict is the same under all three frozen seeds, i.e. the conclusion is not a conclusion about the seed

dataset.coverage_note: Every prime p <= 22000 has a results file.  Above 22000 the release covers only the primes that survive the authors' wisde sieve (a NECESSARY CONDITION for the existence of a curve with delta_E = floor((p/2)^(1/3))), so the p > 22000 sample is SELECTED ON THE UPPER TAIL of the delta distribution.  This is a property of the released data, not a choice of this run.  The frozen contract sweeps 'every prime the dataset covers', so all covered primes enter W-MAIN and W-SENS; the fits restricted to the complete block and to the selected block are recorded separately under robustness_observations.
dataset.origin: github.com/christellevincent/WISDE, folder results/, released with arXiv:2607.14624 (Aubry-Oyono-Vincent)

M_GRAD.reason: M-GRAD requires delta_E along 2-ISOGENY STEPS.  The released dataset carries, per prime, a Z-basis of each maximal order type and its successive minima, but NOT the 2-isogeny adjacency of the supersingular graph. Recovering it would mean enumerating the norm-2 left ideals of each order, computing their right orders, rebuilding each right order's Gross lattice and Eisenstein-reducing it -- i.e. reimplementing the authors' pipeline and GENERATING the neighbour delta values in-session, which is the dependence this experiment exists to escape, and which does not fit the frozen wall-clock budget.  Recorded as a deviation. The arm is exploratory, carries no pre-registered threshold, and no verdict is drawn either way.

estimator_bias_probe.what: The C-NULL surrogate is a random ternary lattice ensemble of determinant ~ p/4.  For such an ensemble the Gaussian heuristic gives #{x : Q(x) <= T}/2 ~ (2*pi/3) T^{3/2} / sqrt(det), i.e. an ASYMPTOTIC alpha of exactly 3/2 and beta of exactly 1/2 BY CONSTRUCTION.  Fitting the frozen estimator over the frozen window to that ensemble therefore measures how far the window's fitted alpha sits from a known true alpha = 3/2.  Recorded as a diagnostic; it enters no verdict.

M_RANGE.resolvable_alpha_difference_at_2se_defin: the smallest |alpha_model - alpha_hat| the fit can exclude at 2 standard errors, i.e. 2 * se(alpha)
M_RANGE.se_caveat: OLS standard errors assume independent cells.  The cells are NESTED CUMULATIVE COUNTS of the same curves (N(T,p) is non-decreasing in T at fixed p), so the residuals are strongly positively autocorrelated along T and these standard errors are ANTI-CONSERVATIVE (too small).  The estimator was frozen in the contract and is reported as frozen; this caveat is recorded, not applied.

normalisation_check.rule: H_reconstructed = #{types: delta=1} + 2*#{types: delta>=2} must equal floor(p/12)+e, e = 0,1,1,2 for p = 1,5,7,11 mod 12

objective_boundary: This run measures a counting function in a published dataset.  It attacks nothing, implements no isogeny algorithm, solves no instance, and produces no evidence about whether a p^{1/4} algorithm exists.
